title: Pullback composition and inverse identities commute with integral scalar extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and $F\in\{E,L\}$ let $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_F)$ be the derived-complete integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and let $T_W:D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_L)$, $K\mapsto K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, be integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For a morphism $f:W'\to W$ of such schemes let $Lf_F^*$ be the integral derived pullback over $\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\alpha^f_K:T_{W'}(Lf_E^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf_L^*(T_WK)$, for $K\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, be the natural scalar-extension comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

Throughout, use the canonical comparison families specified by the whole-system realization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], not arbitrary natural isomorphisms between the same functors.

1. *Composition.* Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be morphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $c^{\mathcal O_F}_{h,k}:L(k\circ h)_F^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_F^*Lk_F^*$ be the integral composition isomorphisms of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition]. Then for every $K\in D^b_c(V,\mathcal O_E)$
$$Lh_L^*(\alpha^k_K)\circ\alpha^h_{Lk_E^*K}\circ T_Z\bigl(c^{\mathcal O_E}_{h,k}(K)\bigr)=c^{\mathcal O_L}_{h,k}(T_VK)\circ\alpha^{k\circ h}_K$$
as isomorphisms $T_Z(L(k\circ h)_E^*K)\to Lh_L^*Lk_L^*(T_VK)$.

2. *Inverse identities along an isomorphism.* Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, with inverse $\bar g:Y\to X$, and write $g^{-1},\bar g^{-1}$ for the inverse-image functors on pro-etale module sheaves [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $F\in\{E,L\}$ and $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_F)$ let $\lambda^g_K:Lg_F^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}K$ and $\lambda^{\bar g}$ be the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], normalized as $(\kappa^{g,F}_K)^{-1}$ and $(\kappa^{\bar g,F})^{-1}$, respectively, where $\kappa$ is the specified quotient-cone map of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), invertible on derived-complete objects by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization]. Let
$$\epsilon^F_K:L\bar g_F^*Lg_F^*K\xrightarrow{\ \lambda^{\bar g}_{Lg_F^*K}\ }\bar g^{-1}Lg_F^*K\xrightarrow{\ \bar g^{-1}(\lambda^g_K)\ }\bar g^{-1}g^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K,$$
the last arrow being the canonical isomorphism of inverse images along $g\circ\bar g=\mathrm{id}_Y$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Then for every $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$
$$\epsilon^L_{T_YK}\circ L\bar g_L^*(\alpha^g_K)\circ\alpha^{\bar g}_{Lg_E^*K}=T_Y(\epsilon^E_K)$$
as isomorphisms $T_Y(L\bar g_E^*Lg_E^*K)\to T_YK$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] to the stated $E\subset L$, $h,k,K$. In its notation take $F_{f,F}=Lf_F^*$ and $a_{f,K}=\alpha^f_K$. Its formulas specify exactly the composition families $c^E,c^L$ and the scalar family in our statement, and its displayed composition/scalar equation is clause (1), with the same source and target. This is an equality obtained from entire quotient diagrams, not an inference from separate finite reductions. No finite Tor-amplitude assumption is required.

proof.text: For clause (2), abbreviate $P_F=Lg_F^*$, $Q_F=L\bar g_F^*$, $G_F=g^{-1}$ and $H_F=\bar g^{-1}$. Both $G_F$ and $H_F$ are the exact site equivalences of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]; write $u_F:H_FG_F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ for their canonical inverse-image identification. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] these functors and $P_F,Q_F$ preserve the stated constructible complete domains. The normalization theorem makes the specified $\kappa$ invertible there; set $\lambda^{g,F}=(\kappa^{g,F})^{-1}$ and likewise for $\bar g$. Thus the defined inverse identity is $\epsilon^F=u_F\circ H_F(\lambda^{g,F})\circ\lambda^{\bar g,F}_{P_F(-)}$, with every component on its required domain.

source.place: First paragraph, inverse automorphism squares and their identity pasting. Stacks 03D6 (sites-modules, definition-pushforward) and 08TC (derived, definition-derived-limit), using the cited specified-comparison normalization.

proof.text: Use $\beta^g:T_XG_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LT_Y$ and $\beta^{\bar g}:T_YH_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H_LT_X$ exactly as defined in [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension]. The comparison $\alpha$ in that node is its specified tensor-and-completion map $Lg_L^*(\chi_Y)[\delta_P]\chi_X^{-1}$; by [lem-pod-isomorphism-scalar-comparison-agreement], applied to $g$ and to $\bar g$, it equals the whole-system scalar comparison $\alpha^g$, resp. $\alpha^{\bar g}$, of our statement. That node therefore gives $\alpha^g T_X(\kappa^{g,E})=\kappa^{g,L}\beta^g$ for our $\alpha^g$. Multiplying by $\lambda^{g,L}$ on the left and by $T_X(\lambda^{g,E})$ on the right gives $\lambda^{g,L}_{T_YK}\alpha^g_K=\beta^g_K T_X(\lambda^{g,E}_K)$. Applying the same statement to $\bar g$ gives $\lambda^{\bar g,L}_{T_XM}\alpha^{\bar g}_M=\beta^{\bar g}_M T_Y(\lambda^{\bar g,E}_M)$. These are cancellation of invertible maps, using the normalization fixed in Step 2.

source.place: First paragraph, inverse automorphism squares. Cancellation of the specified scalar-comparison square, not an additional geometric theorem.

proof.text:
Check the inverse-image counit for these $\beta$ maps. Write $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ and $\chi_W:C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W$ as in [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The cited scalar-comparison node defines $\beta^g=G_L(\chi_Y)b^g\chi_X^{-1}$, and similarly for $\bar g$. In the sectionwise model of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $b$ only reindexes the tensor: $x\otimes a\mapsto g^{-1}(x_0\otimes a_0)$ with the transported coefficient action. Reindexing along $g$ and then $\bar g$ returns both $x$ and $a$ to themselves. Hence on the same complexes $u_{L,C_YK}\,H_L(b^g_K)b^{\bar g}_{G_EK}=C_Y(u_{E,K})$. This equality persists under sheafification and localization because both maps are this identical sectionwise tensor map. Substitute the displayed formulas for $\beta$; the adjacent $H_L(\chi_X^{-1})H_L(\chi_X)$ cancel. Naturality of $u_L$ and then of $\chi_Y$ gives
$$u_{L,T_YK}H_L(\beta^g_K)\beta^{\bar g}_{G_EK}=\chi_{Y,K}C_Y(u_{E,K})\chi_{Y,H_EG_EK}^{-1}=T_Y(u_{E,K}).$$

source.place: First paragraph, inverse square pastes to identity. Explicit cancellation of the tensor/completion conjugations; Stacks 03D6 (sites-modules, definition-pushforward).

proof.text:
Expand the left side of clause (2) using Step 2. Naturality of $\lambda^{\bar g,L}$ for the arrow $\alpha^g_K$, followed by the two equations of Step 3, rewrites it as
$$u_L\,H_L(\beta^g_K)\,H_L(T_X\lambda^{g,E}_K)\,\beta^{\bar g}_{P_EK}\,T_Y(\lambda^{\bar g,E}_{P_EK}).$$
Naturality of $\beta^{\bar g}$ for $\lambda^{g,E}_K:P_EK\to G_EK$ changes the middle pair to $\beta^{\bar g}_{G_EK}\,T_Y(H_E\lambda^{g,E}_K)$. Step 4 now changes the initial triple to $T_Y(u_{E,K})$. Functoriality of $T_Y$ identifies the resulting product with
$$T_Y\bigl(u_{E,K}\circ H_E(\lambda^{g,E}_K)\circ\lambda^{\bar g,E}_{P_EK}\bigr)=T_Y(\epsilon^E_K).$$
The naturality of $\lambda$ is part of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]; that of $\beta$ follows directly from its natural $b,\chi$ formula in [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension]. All these arrows have the source and target displayed in clause (2).
